reason: The global env mutation is real: openbb_mcp.rs and sec_edgar_mcp.rs call set_var/remove_var from two threads spawned in parallel during setup, on edition 2021 where the call is not unsafe. Correction: the two MCP threads racing each other is not the hazard, because std's env functions are synchronised with each other. The Rust docs say the hazard is concurrent reads through non-std getenv (glibc, GTK/WebKit, libc internals). That narrows the risk to C-level readers running at setup time on Linux/macOS; Windows is safe. The fix shape (pass the ports with .env(...) on the sidecar Command) stands.
evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:470-485, src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:59-60,95-96, src-tauri/src/sec_edgar_mcp.rs:58-59,95-96, src-tauri/Cargo.toml:6, rustup toolchain docs share/doc/rust/html/std/env/fn.set_var.html (Safety: 'no other threads concurrently writing or reading(!) the environment through functions or global variables other than the ones in this module'; 'always safe to call on Windows')
evidence_checked: Read the parallel spawn block and every set_var/remove_var site; read the local rustc 1.95 std::env::set_var Safety section.
repro_check: grep -n 'set_var|remove_var' src-tauri/src/*.rs -> 8 sites in openbb_mcp.rs + sec_edgar_mcp.rs; not reproducible as a crash (a timing UB); settled by code + std docs
